filing_playbook.action: Request a written zoning determination from SF Planning Department confirming §231 or §186 applicability and CUA requirements.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a letter to the Planning Department Zoning Administrator requesting a Letter of Determination under Planning Code §311 for 1152 Taylor St. State that the property has an existing restaurant use (cite the 1981 ABC Type 41 license, status REV PENDING) and ask: (1) Does the property qualify under §231 Limited Corner Commercial Use? (2) If not, does the existing restaurant qualify as a Limited Commercial Use under §186 that may continue? (3) Does the proposed enlargement from 1,718 to 2,290 sq ft by merging with an adjacent laundromat space require a Conditional Use Authorization under §202.12 (laundromat removal) and §§180-183 (expansion of non-conforming use)? Request the determination before filing the CUA or building permit.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline is 120–300 days from CUA filing to approval, representing the time to obtain a Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization inferred from comparable case 2015-006347CUA, which took 189 days) and the health permit (14–45 days per catalog sf.health_permit), when they are granted. Cost range covers the CUA application fee (approximately $3,150 in 2023 for a project with tenant improvements, CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 schedule), the building permit with TI ($800–$15,000 per catalog sf.building_permit), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500 per catalog sf.health_plan_check), health permit to operate ($470–$1,000 per catalog sf.health_permit), FOG registration ($0–$500 per catalog sf.fog_wastewater_permit), sign permit ($300–$1,500 per catalog sf.sign_permit), and SF business registration ($55–$700 per catalog sf.business_registration). This timeline and cost apply only if the CUA is approved; they do not cover denial or withdrawal. The timeline does not include pre-application preparation, neighbor outreach or the 30-day appeal period after Commission approval, so plan for an additional 60–90 days before and after the hearing. If the zoning determination in step 1 concludes no CUA is required (for example, if the property qualifies under §231 Limited Corner Commercial Use and the expansion is allowed), the timeline drops to 14–120 days for the building permit and health permit alone, with costs of $800–$15,000 for the building permit, $828–$2,500 for DPH plan check, $470–$1,000 for the health permit, and the other minor fees listed above.

records_summary: The property at 1152 Taylor St is in the RM-3 (Residential-Mixed, Medium Density) zoning district, where restaurants are not a principally permitted use; the Planning Code table has no restaurant row, and retail uses read as not permitted on the first story. However, the site history shows an active Type 41 ABC license (beer and wine, eating place) issued in 1981 to Nob Hill Cafe at 1148 & 1152 Taylor St, currently in "REV PENDING" status, suggesting an existing restaurant use that may qualify under Limited Corner Commercial Use provisions (§231) or continuation of existing use. Within 500 feet there are only 2 registered food/drink businesses and 3 ABC licenses, indicating low density. Recent precedent within 1,000 feet shows Planning approved three restaurant referrals at 1257 Taylor St (112 m away, same RM-3 zoning) in 2022-2023 for a new restaurant, noting the use is "not permitted" but approving ABC licenses anyway, likely under continuation or limited commercial use exceptions.
